push_blocked_reason: A push to main triggers build-image.yml, which republishes the live production image tag (:0.38.0 and :latest) to GHCR. Delivered as pull requests instead.

branches.audit/security-2026-08-03: Tier 1 + Tier 2 fixes, mergeable after ordinary review
branches.audit/money-2026-08-03: Tier 3 money-correctness fixes; do not merge before ACTION_REQUIRED.md section 0

npm_audit.server_after: 1 high (major bump deferred, refuted as exploitable)

findings.title: Three-decimal currencies charged at 1/10 of the displayed amount
findings.summary: Stripe quotes BHD/JOD/KWD/OMR/TND in thousandths and requires a multiple of 10; currencyDecimals returned 2 for them, so a 10.000 KWD donation charged 1.000 KWD while the ledger recorded 10.000. Self-consistent, so only Stripe disagreed.

findings.title: A succeeded one-time charge is never recorded when /confirm does not land
findings.summary: One-time payments are marked succeeded only by the donor browser callback. A closed tab leaves money taken at Stripe and the row pending for ever: no ledger entry, no receipt, no alert, indistinguishable from an abandoned checkout. Monthly plans got reconciliation in v0.38.0; one-time payments did not.

findings.title: Donor-PII CSV export served with no Cache-Control at a .csv URL
findings.summary: The export is every donor name, email and PaymentIntent id, with no cache directives, at an extension Cloudflare caches by default. Behind the tunnel the edge could serve the cached donor list to an unauthenticated request.

findings.title: Image-publishing job runs unpinned third-party Actions while holding GHCR write
findings.summary: Five Actions on moving major tags in a job with packages: write and a GHCR credential for the image every masjid Pi pulls. cla.yml already SHA-pins its action; this file did not.

findings.title: Unauthenticated admin takeover via /api/setup during a platform outage
findings.summary: Under SSO the local admin is never set, so hasAdmin() stays false; the only guard is whether the platform is reachable. During any outage anyone who can reach the box can claim the admin password. Documented in CLAUDE.md as a deliberate anti-bricking tradeoff, so not overridden autonomously.

findings.title: No refund or chargeback handling: local totals permanently overstate income
findings.summary: No refund path in the app and no charge.refunded / charge.dispute.created webhook handling, so a refund issued in the Stripe dashboard never reaches the ledger; metrics, CSV and Gift Aid figures overstate income for ever.

findings.title: Changing the masjid currency rescales every stored amount and misreports history
findings.summary: Amounts are stored in minor units of whatever currency was configured at the time, and rendered with the current currency exponent, so switching currency silently reinterprets every historical row and every configured preset.

findings.title: Cover-the-fees drops the fixed fee for zero-decimal currencies
findings.summary: toMinor(0.30, JPY) rounds to 0, so the +30c half of the 2.9%+0.30 model vanished for all sixteen zero-decimal currencies and the gross-up under-recovered on every covered-fee donation. Also hardcodes a US card rate.

findings.title: All rate limiters collapse to one shared bucket behind the OS ingress
findings.summary: trustProxy is off and every limiter keys on the TCP peer, which is the proxy for all remote visitors. One attacker exhausts the 30/min donation budget for everyone and locks out remote admin logins. The fix needs a platform guarantee about forwarded headers.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /intent creates five persistent Stripe objects with no specific limit
findings.summary: A monthly intent creates a Customer, Price, Subscription, Invoice and PaymentIntent, unauthenticated. A burst bloats the masjid Stripe account and leaves abandoned plan rows behind.

findings.title: No audit log for any admin financial or donor-data action
findings.summary: Nothing recorded who exported the donor ledger, cancelled a plan, rotated a Stripe key or deleted a campaign. A second volunteer with panel access is in the threat model and CLAUDE.md promises a financial record.

findings.title: Admin session cookie never receives Secure, including on HTTPS deployments
findings.summary: secure followed COOKIE_SECURE, which nothing in the repo ever set, while the manifest declares https: true and domain: true. A 30-day admin token was issued with no transport restriction in the normal deployment.

findings.title: No session revocation and no password-change route
findings.summary: A stolen 30-day cookie cannot be invalidated short of deleting the database, and the admin password cannot be changed at all. Needs a token-version scheme plus a change-password route.

findings.title: No security response headers at all
findings.summary: No nosniff, Referrer-Policy or CSP on any route. nosniff and no-referrer shipped; CSP deliberately deferred because a wrong policy stops Stripe Elements and therefore stops donations.

findings.title: Container runs as root with a writable root filesystem
findings.summary: No USER directive, contrary to CLAUDE.md section 10, so the 0600 on the database protects against nothing and an RCE can persist. Needs an entrypoint that chowns /data plus one real container start to verify.

findings.title: Base images pinned by mutable tag, not digest
findings.summary: node:22-slim and cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.6.1 are moving tags, so the same commit does not build the same image. A wrong digest fails the build and the build workflow does not run on pull requests.

findings.title: LoginLimiter sweep condition unreachable, so the map never shrinks
findings.summary: The condition required fails === 0, but an entry only exists after fail() incremented it and succeed() deletes outright, so nothing was ever swept and the map grew one entry per attacking IP for the process lifetime.

findings.title: refresh=1 bypassed the same-origin guard on the plans sync
findings.summary: Only the write side was gated, so a cross-site top-level navigation could still force the cache open and trigger up to 200 outbound Stripe calls.

findings.title: No rate limit on the unauthenticated routes that call the platform outbound
findings.summary: /api/session (SSO branch) and /api/public/appearance each make an outbound call to the OpenMasjidOS core on every request, making the box an unmetered amplifier against the platform.

findings.title: Stripe webhook route unauthenticated with no rate limit
findings.summary: CLAUDE.md section 9 requires a limit. Account resolution can hit the Fabric vault, so an unsigned flood still costs outbound calls.

findings.title: No requestTimeout bound on how long a request may hold a socket
findings.summary: Node defaults already bound the classic slowloris via headersTimeout and a 300s requestTimeout, so this is a tightening to 120s rather than an open hole. Downgraded from the auditor Medium on that basis.

findings.title: Donations log and CSV materialise the whole table with no pagination
findings.summary: Every donation row is loaded into memory on each request. Adding a LIMIT would change the API response and the client-side donor-history panel, so deferred rather than guessed.

findings.title: Donor name reaches the receipt Subject with CR/LF intact
findings.summary: The subject is the admin template with the unauthenticated donor name substituted in, and becomes an SMTP header at the platform, so CR/LF is header injection. Sanitised at the sender; platform counterpart recorded as cross-repo.

findings.title: Anonymous donations de-anonymised by the Stripe billing-name backfill
findings.summary: A donor who deliberately leaves name and email blank has them filled in from Stripe billing details at confirm, so the cardholder name reaches the ledger and the CSV. Genuinely ambiguous intent, so deferred for a decision.

findings.title: No retention limit, deletion path or subject-access export for donor records
findings.summary: Donor records including Gift Aid name and home address are kept indefinitely with no deletion route, and deleting a campaign orphans its donation rows rather than handling them.

findings.title: Cloudflare tunnel token passed in argv, visible in the host process table
findings.summary: Any unprivileged local user on the masjid box can read the tunnel token with ps. Fix is to pass TUNNEL_TOKEN in the child environment, but cloudflared could not be exercised here to confirm.

findings.title: .dockerignore does not exclude .env
findings.summary: COPY server/ ./ would bake a developer local .env, with real Stripe keys, into an image layer where it survives later deletion.

findings.title: SQLite -wal/-shm sidecars escape the 0600 chmod
findings.summary: In WAL mode the newest committed data, including a freshly saved Stripe secret key, lives in the -wal file, which SQLite creates lazily at default permissions. Fixed by locking the directory to 0700 rather than racing the sidecars.

findings.title: No unhandledRejection or uncaughtException handler
findings.summary: The codebase uses fire-and-forget void fn().catch() widely and Node kills the process on an unhandled rejection, so one missed catch in a background alert path would take the donation page down.

findings.title: Upload trusts the client-declared MIME type with no nosniff backstop
findings.summary: A file declared image/png can hold anything and is served from the same origin. Filename and extension are server-chosen, so the residual risk was content sniffing, now closed by nosniff.

findings.title: Duplicate receipt and duplicate alert on concurrent /confirm
findings.summary: The wasPending guard is a read-then-write with no transaction, so two concurrent confirms can both see pending and both send. Fix needs an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE status = pending, which changes how a donation is recorded.

findings.title: invoice.paid reads Invoice fields Stripe removed in 2025-03-31.basil
findings.summary: The webhook casts the event to a hand-written shape, so TypeScript cannot catch drift. Latent today (SDK 17.7 speaks acacia) but a routine bump to 18.x would silently stop recording monthly renewals with no error.

findings.title: Gift Aid is dead plumbing and the flag is client-settable with no declaration
findings.summary: The flag is stored and sent to Stripe as metadata but no declaration, name or address is ever collected, and any unauthenticated client can set it. A masjid could file a claim on donations with no declaration behind them.

findings.title: Idempotency keys are freshly random per request, so they dedupe nothing
findings.summary: crypto.randomUUID() per request means a client retry of the same logical donation creates a second PaymentIntent, contrary to the intent of CLAUDE.md section 9.

findings.title: The 99,999,999 ceiling is validated pre-fee, so the gross-up can exceed it
findings.summary: The maximum is checked on the base amount; a cover-the-fees gross-up can then push the charged amount above Stripe limit, which fails at Stripe rather than being caught with a friendly message.

findings.title: The per-currency minimum charge is a stub with both branches equal
findings.summary: currencyDecimals(currency) === 0 ? 50 : 50 — the ternary was never finished, so a zero-decimal currency uses the same floor as a two-decimal one.

findings.title: The monthly confirm dialog states the pre-fee amount as the recurring charge
findings.summary: With cover-the-fees on, the donor is shown the base amount as what will recur monthly while the gross-up is what is actually charged each month.

findings.title: Months grouped in UTC but windowed in local time; MASJID_TIMEZONE unused
findings.summary: strftime groups created_at in UTC while the six-month window is built from the server local clock, and the platform-provided timezone is never applied, so a donation near midnight can land in the wrong month.

findings.title: Historical amounts formatted with the current currency exponent
findings.summary: The ledger and CSV convert every stored row using the currently configured currency decimals rather than the exponent of the currency the row was taken in.

findings.title: @fastify/static carries four High advisories, not exploitable in this configuration
findings.summary: REFUTED as reachable by the adversarial pass: both registrations set index: false and never list: true, both roots hold only already-public assets, and every protected route is a Fastify route with a preHandler rather than a static route guard. Fix is a two-major bump.

findings.title: Three transitive High advisories with non-major fixes available
findings.summary: brace-expansion, fast-uri and find-my-way. All unreachable as configured (no HTTP/2, no attacker-controlled URI parsing), but the fixes were free.

findings.title: postcss advisory is build-time only
findings.summary: A devDependency that never ships, processing only first-party CSS. Fixed anyway; web audit is now zero vulnerabilities.

findings.title: No scheduled dependency-audit workflow
findings.summary: The only workflow was the release image build, so a new advisory against fastify, better-sqlite3 or the Stripe SDK went unnoticed until someone ran npm audit by hand.

findings.title: stripe.ts, every money conversion in the product, had zero tests
findings.summary: No test covered currencyDecimals, toMinor, toMajor or withCoveredFees, and no route or integration test exists at all. The new suite is what surfaced DONATIONS-001 and -008 as reproducible.

findings.title: i18n and RTL are aspirational despite the stated requirement
findings.summary: CLAUDE.md section 12 requires RTL-ready with logical CSS properties. In practice all strings are inline English, no dir or lang is set, and the platform lang hand-off is ignored, so an Arabic locale would not render correctly today.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md specifies argon2; the implementation is scrypt
findings.summary: scrypt at N=2^16 with a per-hash cost record is a sound choice; the documentation was wrong, not the code.

findings.title: Uploaded images are never deleted when a campaign is deleted
findings.summary: deleteCampaign drops the row and leaves the files on the data volume, so an admin editing images repeatedly grows the volume with no way to reclaim it from the panel.

findings.title: /api/app discloses the platform internal LAN address to the public
findings.summary: omosBase is returned to unauthenticated visitors, revealing the internal address of the OpenMasjidOS core to anyone who can load the donation page.

findings.title: docker-compose.yml deviates from the catalog contract
findings.summary: None of the three required com.openmasjid.* labels are present and the host port is hardcoded rather than using the platform-assigned variable. Part of the published catalog contract, so cross-repo.

findings.title: Code health: a 2,262-line route file, duplicated logic, dead exports
findings.summary: index.ts holds every route, the outboxes, the caches and the static host. Three pieces of duplicated logic and two dead exports. No TODO/FIXME anywhere and full SPDX coverage, which is unusually good.

findings.title: Any platform-authenticated identity becomes a full local admin
findings.summary: GET /api/session mints an admin session for any identity the platform confirms; the username is recorded but never checked against a role. If OpenMasjidOS gains non-admin users they silently become donations administrators.

findings.title: Outbox passes have no overlap guard, so a slow provider causes duplicate sends
findings.summary: Both outboxes run on a 60s interval and each item makes an 8s-timeout network call, so a pass can outlast its own interval, and a second pass then reads the same pending rows and repeats the work.
